pr_title: Adding support for exist queries to sparse_vector fields
pr_body:
In this PR we want to add support for `exists` queries to the `sparse_vector` fields, so that one can find easily documents missing values for the specific field type (e.g. to identify potential issues with inference/ingestion pipelines). 

To do this, we rely on the existing work for a common way of expressing `exists` queries in different mappers (introduced in PR #57607) and make use of the `_field_names` field, if and only if, the provided vector has defined at least one strictly positive dimension defined. 

Closes #99319

issue_context.title: sparse_vector fields should support exists queries
comments:
When the initial implementation for `sparse_vectors` was added, we specified them having `docValues=True` and `isIndexed=False` (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/57607 & https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/62631) in an effort to also support a common way for expressing & evaluating `exists` queries for different mappers.  

In https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/98996 where we moved the `sparse_vector` back from being deprecated, we copied it over from `RankFeaturesField` which at the time was an indexed field (as per https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/93247). 

How do we expect the `sparse_vector` field to be used, so that we can make sure that it is properly configured? If we keep  the properties as they are (i.e. `isIndexed=True` & `docValues=False`) we can simply remove the override to `existsQuery`, add the field to the `_field_names` iff it has any non-zero values, and fall back to the base class' implementation in `org.elasticsearch.index.mapper.MappedFieldType#existsQuery` (as also per the effort in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/57607). WDYT?

I am not sure `exists` works currently as is or not, I am guessing it doesn't. Right now we don't support `docValues`, and I am not sure we will for this mapping type.

I think adding to the `_fields_names` makes the most sense to me.

review_comments:
I **think**  we need to introduce a new index version, because we are changing  the index data (adding a new data to `_field_names`). If there was an index created after `NEW_SPARSE_VECTOR_INDEX_VERSION`, but before this change, we still can't use `exists` query on it.

@benwtrent What do you think? Does it warrant a new index version?
@mayya-sharipova it does warrant a new index version.
Ah fair enough! I was under the impression that it'd need a new index version if the changes didn't make it into the same release (i.e. waiting until Oct 3).

If the field was created in an 8.11 index, we should probably still throw here. We never want to get in the scenario where some `sparse_vector` match `exists` and others do not in the same index. 

That would be confusing.
NOTE: This is irrelevant of 8.11 or not. Its a NEW commit and a new change. We should handle this correctly given the new `IndexVersion` format.
Yeap, makes sense. I was considering that "some" results would still be valid, but the response will be inconsistent. Will update as suggested.
